A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete versions of the same RTO paper. Text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support reliable comparison. The summarization material moves from Appendix E to Appendix F without substantive deletion.

before.justification: Section 5 reports original alignment experiments on AlpacaEval 2 and Arena-Hard; Appendix E reports original TL;DR summarization experiments.

after.justification: The original experiments remain, with summarization in Appendix F. New Appendix E additionally reports REINFORCE++ and RTO with REINFORCE++ results.

M1.justification: Appendix E adds RTO(RPP), applying the existing token-reward mechanism through REINFORCE++ instead of PPO. This introduces a practical optimization variant described as using discounted returns without a critic. The original reward construction and Algorithms 1–2 remain unchanged.

E1.justification: UltraFeedback alignment, AlpacaEval 2, Arena-Hard, and TL;DR summarization coverage remain unchanged. The added RPP experiment changes the optimizer within existing benchmark coverage.

E2.justification: New Appendix E evaluates REINFORCE++ (RPP) against RTO(RPP), alongside existing SFT, DPO, PPO, and RTO(PPO) results. The comparator sets in the original benchmark and summarization comparisons remain intact.

E3.justification: The new RPP comparison introduces critic-free training configurations, with both variants reporting actor learning rate 5e-7, batch size 128, and 1024-token prompt and response limits. Existing experimental settings, metrics, and summarization evaluation procedures remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix E adds a generality test asking whether token rewards remain beneficial with an optimizer other than PPO. Existing reward-granularity, reward-shaping, data-scaling, temperature, and optimization-curve analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports empirical repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The added comparison continues the existing practice of reporting point estimates.

E6.justification: New Table 2 adds RPP/RTO(RPP) scores: AlpacaEval LC 18.28/24.71 and WR 13.91/23.11; Arena-Hard SC 13.4/18.8 and WR 15.4/21.8. These are additional configurations, not revised scores for existing experiments. Previously reported results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The MDP definitions, assumptions, reward derivations, sample-complexity results, and proofs in Sections 3–4 and Appendices A–C are unchanged. The new RPP appendix adds no formal result.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about token-wise MDP modeling, sample-efficient RTO, and the practical DPO–PPO combination. The new experiment does not redefine these core contributions.

C2.justification: Appendix E newly interprets the results as evidence of applicability beyond PPO and tentatively attributes PPO's advantage to its critic capturing fine-grained information. That mechanism is not isolated experimentally, and the reported rankings vary across metrics.

D1.justification: Two new configuration tables document RPP and RTO(RPP), including learning rates, batch sizes, length limits, and reward/KL coefficients. Existing implementation and access information remain unchanged. The new tables retain unexplained PPO and GAE labels despite describing critic-free discounted-return training.

R1.justification: v4 adds Hu (2025), REINFORCE++, to support the new optimizer comparison. Existing references and the substantive related-work discussion remain unchanged.

P1.justification: v4 expands the closing experimental paragraph, inserts the REINFORCE++ appendix, relabels summarization as Appendix F, updates cross-references, and changes the revision date. The existing scientific narrative is largely unchanged.

P2.justification: v4 adds one results table and two configuration tables. Existing summarization tables are renumbered, Figures 5–6 are grouped on page 26, and subsequent appendix content is rearranged. The existing plots and their contents are retained.

improvement.justification: v3's practical experiments used PPO; v4's new Table 2 provides a useful additional test showing token-reward benefits with REINFORCE++ on both controlled benchmarks. This modestly strengthens empirical support for broader applicability. Unexplained PPO/GAE configuration labels and the speculative critic explanation limit the gain.
